Birzai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Biržai's Jewish community, dating to the 17th century, was reportedly invited by Prince Christopher Radziwiłł to promote local economic development; Karaites settled first, with Rabbinic Jews arriving only in the century's middle decades. The population reached 2,510 of 4,413 residents (57 percent) by 1897, engaged mainly in the flax and timber trade, and producing white linen renowned across the region. The town's most famous rabbi, Elchonon Bunim Wasserman — one of the closest students of the Chofetz Chaim and a prominent rosh yeshiva in prewar Europe — served there, and Biržai was also home to Herbert Kretzmer, the English journalist and lyricist best known for his English-language lyrics to Les Misérables. On August 8, 1941, 2,400 Jewish men, women, and children were shot in two forest pits outside the city; a 2019 Holocaust memorial there, designed by South African architect Dr. Joseph Rabie — whose own great-grandparents came from Biržai — etches 2,400 Stars of David and 522 identified victims' names into metal sheets across a bridge spanning the death pits. This is one of the largest and most studied Jewish cemeteries in Lithuania, established at the beginning of the 17th century and holding 1,627 tombstones.
